counterevidence: Cedar tried foreign list requests once before any useful own retained copies were present. Wider permissions may initially reveal empty listings and need not produce later revisits.
Juniper and Willow queried only their own processors despite observing the inventory; permission availability does not imply discovery or sustained exchange.

Ordinary owner briefs cover disjoint customer rosters and omit the private foreign facts needed by another owner. In the accepted content case Cedar/Willow independently added source_documents; this candidate supplies no such convention and publishes no private source data automatically.
The change adds a content route rather than increasing the capacity of the identifier carrier. Classifying future retained-copy transfers as metadata would be wrong.
Shared group write also opens untested foreign submissions and reply injection; queue ownership cannot be used as author identity.
No model evidence or new negative/positive verdict exists for this candidate. The documented refinement count remains two until a fresh registered rollout is reviewed.
